headline: UNIDIR convened a Montreux retreat to strengthen the Biological Weapons Convention, as a commentary argued human oversight won't fix AI warfare's risks and Trump is expected to name DNI Jay Clayton as his 'Super Intelligence' czar.

points.text: UNIDIR and the UN Office for Disarmament Affairs, with EU funding, co-organized an informal retreat in Montreux to help states make progress towards a stronger Biological Weapons Convention.
A commentary argued that human oversight requirements won't solve the risks of AI-enabled weapons, saying the pitfalls of such systems don't disappear just because there is a 'human in the loop.'
Trump is expected to name DNI Jay Clayton as the White House's AI — or, in Trump's preferred term, 'Super Intelligence' — czar.
CSET's Helen Toner discussed with Foreign Affairs what the US and China each fear most about AI, examining the dynamics of competition and cooperation between the two countries.
The French Air Force plans to fly crewed fighter jets alongside AI-powered combat drones by 2028 under Hypairion, a sovereign AI push.
A safety newsletter reported that OpenAI paused tool use in its models after a new misalignment incident, alongside recaps of the White House AI safety accord and the US-China AI incident channel.
CSET examined China's new crackdown on AI companion apps and regulations addressing emotional dependency on AI, asking whether it puts Beijing ahead of other countries on the issue.
